name: Fine-Tuning Orchestrator
description: Orchestrates the fine-tuning process when triggered by the training data store. Behind a FineTuneBackend protocol/ABC with implementations: UnslothBackend (local LoRA fine-tuning), OpenAIBackend (OpenAI fine-tuning API), HuggingFaceBackend (Hugging Face Trainer). For local backends: manages the full pipeline of train → quantize → GGUF conversion (via llama.cpp quantize) → register with Ollama (ollama create with Modelfile). Handles fine-tuning as a blocking operation. On failure: logs error, keeps current model version, schedules retry on next batch. Produces a ModelVersion artifact with full provenance metadata.

functions.name: fine_tune
functions.description: Core protocol method on FineTuneBackend. Executes a fine-tuning run against the configured backend. For local backends (Unsloth, HuggingFace), this internally runs the full pipeline: train → quantize → GGUF convert → Ollama register. For remote backends (OpenAI), this uploads training data, triggers the job, polls for completion, and returns the result. This is an async blocking operation — it awaits the full fine-tuning process before returning. The backend must not raise exceptions for fine-tuning failures; all errors are returned as FineTuneError within the FineTuneResult union.

inputs.name: request
inputs.description: The fine-tuning request containing training examples, base model, and optional hyperparameter overrides.

error_cases.name: training_failed
error_cases.condition: Backend training process fails (e.g. OOM, CUDA error, API rejection)

error_cases.name: quantization_failed
error_cases.condition: llama.cpp quantize subprocess fails (local backends only)

error_cases.name: ollama_registration_failed
error_cases.condition: ollama create command fails or Ollama HTTP API is unreachable (local backends only)

error_cases.name: api_rate_limited
error_cases.condition: Remote API returns rate limit / quota exceeded (OpenAI backend)

error_cases.name: api_timeout
error_cases.condition: Remote API fine-tuning job exceeds poll_timeout_seconds

error_cases.name: invalid_training_data
error_cases.condition: Backend rejects training data format or content

error_cases.name: model_not_found
error_cases.condition: Base model identifier is not recognized by the backend

error_cases.name: authentication_failed
error_cases.condition: API key missing, invalid, or expired (remote backends)

preconditions: request.base_model is a valid model identifier recognized by the backend
request.run_id is a unique, non-empty string
postconditions: Returns ModelVersion with status='success' if fine-tuning completed successfully
Returns FineTuneError with status='error' if fine-tuning failed for any reason
On success, ModelVersion.artifact_location points to a valid, accessible model artifact
On success for local backends, ModelVersion.ollama_model_name is set and the model is registered with Ollama
ModelVersion.training_example_ids matches the example_id values from the input request
ModelVersion.training_example_count equals len(request.training_examples)
ModelVersion.run_id matches request.run_id
No exception is raised — all errors are captured in FineTuneError

For local backends: registers model via Ollama API or CLI.

functions.name: trigger_fine_tuning
functions.description: Main entry point on FineTuningOrchestrator. Called when a new batch of training examples is available. Validates the batch meets minimum size requirements, generates a run_id, constructs a FineTuneRequest, invokes the injected FineTuneBackend, and handles the result. On success: persists the ModelVersion via ModelVersionStore and returns it. On failure: logs the error, keeps current model version unchanged, and returns the FineTuneError. This is the coordinating function that wraps the backend call with orchestration logic.

invariants: FineTuneBackend protocol implementations must never raise exceptions for fine-tuning failures — all errors are returned as FineTuneError within the FineTuneResult union
ModelVersion.training_example_ids always matches the example_ids from the FineTuneRequest that produced it, in the same order
ModelVersion.version_id is globally unique across all stored versions (UUID4)
ModelVersion.started_at < ModelVersion.completed_at for all successful fine-tuning runs
On fine-tuning failure, the current active model version is never modified or invalidated
Consecutive failure count is incremented on each failure and reset to 0 on success
All structured log entries within a fine-tuning run include the same fine_tune_run_id correlation field
Config parsing fails fast at startup with clear error messages — never silently defaults to fallback values
CommandRunner.run_command never raises exceptions — all failures are captured in CommandResult.return_code
For local backends (Unsloth, HuggingFace), a successful ModelVersion always has a non-empty ollama_model_name
For local backends, the full pipeline (train → quantize → GGUF → Ollama register) must complete for the result to be ModelVersion; partial completion results in FineTuneError
ModelVersionStore operations are safe for sequential access — no concurrent write guarantees required (fine-tuning is blocking)
BackendConfig discriminated union is resolved exactly by the backend_type literal field
No global state — all state flows through explicit constructor parameters or injected dependencies
